name: productivity_sdk

database._comment_migration:
THE MIGRATION VERSION NUMBER IS SHARED WITH EVERY OTHER SDK IN THE APP, AND IS NOT THIS SDK'S TO COUNT ALONE. The composer sets the composed AppDatabase's schemaVersion to the MAXIMUM version any composed manifest declares (sdk_installer_base.py update_database_registration) while each SDK writes its own `if (from < N)` guards, so the numbers live in one namespace with no allocator. auth_sdk (Users/auth/dart/manifest.json) already declares 16 for offlineUsersTable, so the composed launcher was ALREADY at schemaVersion 16 while this manifest still said 15 - and the 1.6.0 bump 15 -> 16 therefore raised nothing. Drift only calls onUpgrade when schemaVersion is greater than the stored user_version, so on any device that had the previous launcher installed no upgrade ran at all, notes_table was never created, and every note insert failed on `no such table`. Notes are created at 17 for that reason. When adding a table here, claim a version HIGHER than any other composed manifest's - never merely one above this SDK's own last number.

OWNER SCOPING, VERSION 20 (2026-09-20). Every table this manifest registers gained an `owner` column IN ITS PRIMARY KEY, so two accounts on one device cannot see each other's rows - the follow-up to core PR #254, which did the same for base_sdk's KeyValueTable and OutboxTable at version 19. 20 was reserved for this change fleetwide and is above every number in the field (base_sdk 19, radio_sdk 18, this SDK's own previous 17, auth_sdk 16). VISIBILITY SCOPING, NEVER DELETION: the step destroys nothing and guesses no owner - carried-over rows take the '' default and come out UNOWNED, which the visibility rule `owner = '' OR owner = <me>` treats as the current account's, so every row already on a device stays exactly as visible as it is today. The step rebuilds each table the long way round (rename aside, create from the current Dart definition, copy the shared columns, drop) because SQLite cannot alter a primary key in place; ensureProductivityOwnerColumns() lives in tasks_table.dart because the composer copies only the files named under `tables` into base_sdk's package, and it is idempotent, so running it here, in this SDK's own floor (ProductivityOwnerScope.ready, awaited by every read and write) or in both comes to the same thing. notes_table's create moved from `from < 17` to this step for the rule the test below pins: the newest work is done at the top version, so no device sits between the two numbers and misses it. KNOWN PRE-EXISTING COLLISION, not fixed here: radio_sdk (RokctAI/agent radio/dart) also declares 17, the number this manifest used to hold.

migration.step: if (from < 13) { await m.createTable(tasksTable); } if (from < 14) { await m.createTable(recoveryProfilesTable); await m.createTable(avoidedHabitsTable); await m.createTable(urgeLogsTable); await m.createTable(dailyRitualsTable); await m.createTable(ritualLogsTable); await m.createTable(procrastinationLogsTable); } if (from < 15) { await m.addColumn(tasksTable, tasksTable.clientId); await m.addColumn(tasksTable, tasksTable.remoteId); } if (from < 20) { await m.createTable(notesTable); await ensureProductivityOwnerColumns(this, <TableInfo<Table, dynamic>>[tasksTable, notesTable, recoveryProfilesTable, avoidedHabitsTable, urgeLogsTable, dailyRitualsTable, ritualLogsTable, procrastinationLogsTable]); }

_comment_boot_hooks:
This SDK's half of a sign-out, and it deletes NOTHING. Ray, 2026-09-19: "if on temp local user you logout all your tasks still show" - the symptom was that the rows were still PAINTED, not that they were still on disk. tasksStateProvider is a plain StateNotifierProvider, root-scoped and not autoDispose, so the notifier and the tasks it holds outlive the replaceMainRoute a sign-out ends with: the page is rebuilt and re-reads the same surviving notifier. ProductivitySessionEnd.clearLiveView empties every live notifier (TasksNotifier.clearLive) and drops the transient TaskPullService.lastFailure notice that belonged to the session that just ended. Two in-memory writes; no store write, no network call. Registration is idempotent by id, so a hot restart or a host calling the hook twice cannot stack duplicates, and the hook is inert until a sign-out actually happens.

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DELETE: anything. Not the tasks rows, not the notes rows, not this SDK's pending outbox rows, not the pull cursor, not the recovery tables. Ray's ruling on the first cut of this hook, which did delete all of those: a local temp account that does real work and signs out must not come back to an empty list, and the same holds for a seller. The pending outbox rows are the sharpest case - they are work the user did that has not reached the server yet, so deleting them destroys it outright. Emptying the screen is reversible; emptying the tables is not.

WHAT IS THEREFORE STILL OPEN, named rather than left unsaid: this clears the session, not the ownership. One device shared by two accounts still shows each the other's rows once the tables are read again, because TasksTable.createdBy is written and never filtered on and NotesTable has no user column at all. The fix for that is owner scoping - a WHERE at the repository layer and a migration for notes - not a wipe at sign-out.

No 'imports' entry, for the same reason auth_sdk's restore-credential hook declares none: every composed main.dart already imports package:productivity_sdk/productivity_sdk.dart (this barrel exports ProductivitySessionEnd) and package:users_sdk/users_sdk.dart (which exports SessionEndHooks) in its @generated-sdk-imports block, and a wiring-block duplicate would trip duplicate_import in every app.

Naming users_sdk from a productivity_sdk hook does NOT create a package dependency: the body is HOST code, and this package's pubspec still depends on nothing but base_sdk. It does mean the hook only composes alongside users_sdk - which is every app that can sign a user out, since users_sdk is what owns logout. A future compose that mounts this SDK with no users_sdk would need the hook moved behind an app_type gate; there is no such compose today.
_comment_tr_keys: Design strip section 47 (47a-47d, 47h, 47i): the compose lane's 'From template' row and its six chips, plus the one line frame 47d's gate says under them while the plant is not yet described. The composer injects these into base_sdk's TrKeys, so the installed tasks page reads them as TrKeys.<name>; this SDK's own lib never references them (its tests run on a bare checkout). Checked against base_sdk's hand-written keys and every other SDK manifest in the fleet: no collision. The step names and instructions inside the templates are DATA on the task map (paas_pos's own strings, verbatim), not copy, and  carry no key. The last two are the /tasks plus's own label on the floating nav - the string base_sdk reads out as `Semantics(label:)` and shows as the long-press `Tooltip(message:)`, which is exactly what adaptive_bar.md §8 reaches: no hardcoded user-facing strings, INCLUDING accessibility labels. `ProductivityPlusNav` asks for these two BY VALUE rather than as `TrKeys.<name>`, because this SDK's lib runs on a bare checkout where nothing has been injected - the same shape launch_sdk's `LauncherAppItem` uses for `use_as_phone`. Unserved, `AppHelpers.humanizeTrKey` renders them New task and New note, the words the new-item sheet already uses, so English is unchanged and only other locales gain.
_comment_routes_vision: Design strip section 41 (the M2 vision cluster, approved 2026-08-30): /vision hosts the plan on a page (41a) with the objective drill in its last plane (41b) and the stacked phone fold (41d); /vision/mastery hosts personal mastery (41c). Both are pushed pages from the productivity gate (approved 7e) and draw the corner back pill themselves. View-first: they read the productivity module's six get_* methods through the platform gateway and write nothing - the legacy add/edit dialogs are write endpoints to add at build time. Other SDKs open them by route path and never import productivity_sdk (ADR-005).
_comment_routes: Design strip section 46: /tasks/run?task=<id> hosts a task's guided run as a page of its own. On a wide window /tasks hosts the same TaskRunView in its detail plane (frame 46a, no new push; frame 47a, no new plane), and the route itself hands a wide window to that workspace with the run open rather than claiming planes of its own; at one plane the workspace pushes this route (46f). Other SDKs open a run by route path and never import productivity_sdk (ADR-005). At one plane it pops true when the user marks the task done from the finished card; on a wide window the workspace ticks the task itself.
_comment_integrations_vision: Design strip section 41: the two vision pages ride the same launcher glance entry as /tasks. As of 1.6.2 they ride it as ATTENTION, not as doors: ProductivityAttention reads only fields these doctypes already carry - and they carry no dates at all (flag (b): no objective status or dates, no goal status), so the plan asks for an objective no KPI measures and mastery asks for an open ToDo row whose date has arrived. Same route-path navigation, same missing-marker skip. The hub-side door - rows under the productivity group of the manager hub (approved 7e) - is the COMMERCE side of the section, like the tasks-row markers below, and is not in this release.
_comment_integrations: When the host also composes launch_sdk (its installed home page ships the '// @launcher-glance' marker at lib/presentation/pages/launch/home.dart, and the '// @launcher-glance-imports' marker at column 0 among its imports), inject NeedsAttentionGlance there. As of 1.6.2 this is ONE widget that shows WHAT NEEDS ATTENTION, not three permanent doors (Ray, 2026-09-19: "in home the glance has 3 items, task, plan on a page, personal mastery. all these are  productivity. having a productivity button in floating nav is better and the glance show what need attention") - the three doors are one Productivity entry on launch_sdk 1.7.5's floating nav, and this glance shows the tasks, plan objectives and mastery to-dos that actually want the reader, and NOTHING at all when none do (base_sdk GlanceCard collapses on an empty item list). Two entries now, exactly like the tasks-row pair below: the line is this SDK's own widget and the launcher home does not import productivity_sdk on its own, so the imports marker takes the import and the glance marker takes the widget. The widget placeholder is still the marker line INCLUDING its 12-space indent: update_layout_integrations() does a plain substring replace, and the bare marker text is also a prefix of the '// @launcher-glance-imports' marker at column 0, which the indent keeps it from matching. Navigation is still by ROUTE PATH through context.router, which the launch home template already imports, so this SDK still never imports launch_sdk (ADR-005). In hosts without launch_sdk the target file does not exist and both integrations are skipped.
_comment_integrations_tasks_row: Design strip frame 46i (approved 2026-08-30; 47j folded into it 2026-08-31): the paused run announces itself on the door it lives behind - ONE LINE on the hub's existing Tasks row, not a new row and not a new group, gone when no run is paused. When the host composes merchants_sdk (its installed manager hub ships the '// @productivity-tasks-row' marker under the Tasks row of lib/presentation/pages/manager/restaurant/restaurant_page.dart, plus '// @productivity-tasks-row-imports' at column 0 among its imports), inject PausedRunLine there. Two entries because the line is this SDK's widget and the hub does not import productivity_sdk on its own: the imports marker takes the import, the row marker takes the widget. Same substring-replace rules as the launcher glance: the row placeholder carries its 8-space indent so it cannot match the column-0 imports marker, of which the bare marker text is a prefix. The line opens the run by ROUTE PATH ('/tasks/run?task=<id>', this SDK's own route) through context.router, which the hub already imports, so the hub never imports a page (ADR-005). Both markers are the COMMERCE side of the frame and land in the merchants repo; until they do, the composer reports the marker missing and skips the wiring, exactly as it does for a host without launch_sdk.
